solutionMethods.explanation:
The constant term is the only term of a polynomial that remains when \(x=0\), since all positive powers of \(x\) vanish. Therefore the constant term of \((x+1)^6\) is
\[
(0+1)^6=1.
\]

Method 1: Select the term with no x

The constant term contains no \(x\), meaning the exponent of \(x\) is 0. Its coefficient is \(C(6,6)=1\).

Method 2: Evaluate at zero

The constant term is the only term of a polynomial that remains when \(x=0\), since all positive powers of \(x\) vanish. Therefore the constant term of \((x+1)^6\) is
\[
(0+1)^6=1.
\]

nodes.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms.
